hypotheses.claim: Timing-sensitive causal-emergence readouts can be biased when observation overhead/jitter is non-negligible relative to decision or re-entry slack.
hypotheses.prediction: Instrumented H1 episodes near timing boundaries show larger semantic/readout divergence than high-slack episodes under matched common snapshots.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Current observability overhead is too small or sufficiently out-of-band to change FRANK semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across preregistered stress regimes, probe mode/density causes no material event-order, semantic-outcome, or emergence-readout divergence within tolerance.

hypotheses.claim: Aggregate distribution equivalence can hide paired trajectory divergence caused by instrumentation.
hypotheses.prediction: Some symmetric-probe conditions preserve aggregate winner/outcome rates while flipping individual episode winners/orderings.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Aggregate equality is sufficient evidence of measurement noninterference.
hypotheses.falsifier: Whenever aggregate metrics remain invariant, paired episode identities/orderings also remain invariant within tolerance.

hypotheses.claim: Probe-effect risk scales with proximity to timing/selection boundaries, not just absolute instrumentation overhead.
hypotheses.prediction: The same added delay produces substantially larger relative outcome loss as baseline timing slack approaches zero.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Probe effect is approximately uniform across timing margins.
hypotheses.falsifier: Sensitivity curves show no meaningful interaction between baseline slack and probe overhead.

hypotheses.claim: A backend's disabled/armed state must be empirically classified; logging-off cannot be assumed zero-effect.
hypotheses.prediction: Some tracing modes retain measurable overhead when event emission is disabled/paused, while others approach zero-effect.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: All planned observability backends are effectively noninterfering when emission is disabled.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target-host calibration shows disabled/armed modes indistinguishable from no instrumentation across timing, scheduling, and semantic outcomes.
